The reserved-prefix 400 passes on a plain and an unheld role topic with the expected list asserted. vet clean, listener+logging+bus suites green, round-1 lines 1-4 still pass, CI green at 251fbd90, MERGEABLE, no .omp/config.yml. Two findings: (1) review round 1's body finding 4 — packages/envoy/docs/architecture.md lines 74 and 86 — did not land (still 'delivery_failed' for a receipt timeout, two reasons); (2) the flush-failure branch of RequestCoreTo has no regression lock in the committed suite (my fault injection there stayed green everywhere; only my throwaway probe caught it). documentationFeedback: packages/envoy/AGENTS.md is accurate. docs/solutions/architecture-patterns/core-nats-receipt-backed-current-holder-delivery.md has two wording defects the reviewer should weigh (neither changes behaviour): (a) the 'Correct: require the selected receiver to reply' Go snippet (lines 86-93) still maps every RequestCoreTo error to publishDeliveryException(..., "delivery_failed"), contradicting the sentence immediately below it at line 107 ('observable as receipt_timeout (fresh but deaf) and delivery_failed (stopped)') — a reader copying the 'Correct' pattern reproduces the pre-LEGION-108 bug; the snippet needs an errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) -> receipt_timeout branch. (b) line 35's parenthetical 'the receiver has the envelope and has not acknowledged it — a slow holder, not a lost message' overstates: a holder whose session-registry entry is inside ClaimStaleAfter (5 min, internal/session/claim.go:13) but whose process is gone also gets receipt_timeout, and it never had the envelope (RequestCoreTo publishes to a subject with no subscriber and times out). AGENTS.md's phrasing — 'the message was forwarded and not acknowledged; the Legion daemon treats it as delivered to a live process' — is the accurate one and the parent contract (daemon probes on receipt_timeout) covers the dead-but-fresh case.
observations: The implementer's handoff proof was complete and reproduced exactly; every reason assertion in the four line-2 tests is on the exact reason string (grep of assertDeliveryException calls), not merely 'an exception'.

RequestCoreTo never uses nats.Conn.Request, so ErrNoResponders cannot appear; a deaf subject is indistinguishable from a slow one at the listener and both are receipt_timeout by design of the parent contract.

Test wall time for the first test in a go test process includes the shared nats:2.10 testcontainer's creation; Docker on this box took between ~1s and ~42s for that step across runs. The receipt_timeout tests' bodies are ~3s each, bounded by the 2s roleReceiptTimeout.
